PURPOSE.what_this_amendment_does: Consumes the executor-hardening FAIL, replaces the verdict-NAME predicate of LIMB_1 with a certification-SEMANTICS predicate bound to the exact candidate, records the execution-hardening corrections the IC's findings called for, and corrects three measured factual errata of v1.0.4.
what_it_does_not_do: It adds no read, widens no allowlist, relaxes no prohibition and takes no owner decision.
It does not redesign the authority: the registry, the terminating DN-0 protocol and AC-1 are unchanged in concept.
It does not arm anything. Arming remains a runtime evaluation of AC-1 on every execution.

CERTIFICATION_PREDICATE.why_the_name_predicate_was_wrong: The verdict NAMESPACE is the certifier's choice. The v1.0.4 code bound LIMB_1 to a namespace the AUTHOR guessed, so a faithful materialization of a PASS by the actual certifier (namespace INFRA_CONTROL_PLANE_READ_EXECUTOR_HARDENING_IC_*) could never arm. Teaching the code the other spelling would repeat the defect for the next certifier: the namespace would become an accidental ABI.
CERTIFICATION_PREDICATE.rule: NORMATIVE. A certification event satisfies LIMB_1 for a requirement {path, packageId, certifiedCandidate} if and only if ALL of: (1) it parses as a JSON object; (2) authority_class begins with INDEPENDENT_CERTIFICATION_EVENT_RECORD (document class); (3) package_id equals the requirement's packageId (the event the MATERIALIZER was told to write; chosen by the materializer, never by the reviewer); (4) CERTIFIED_CANDIDATE.candidate_head is a full 40-hex SHA equal to the requirement's certifiedCandidate; (5) VERDICT.blocking_findings is the integer 0; (6) VERDICT.verdict is a single upper-case token whose TERMINAL class is PASS or PASS_WITH_NONBLOCKING_FINDINGS, and none of whose namespace tokens is a failure or negation token. The certified candidate must also be an ancestor of the executing HEAD.
never_satisfies_it: a PASS for a different candidate (candidate check)
a PASS for another artifact class or another event (package_id and document-class checks)
prose containing the word PASS (single-token rule)
a FAIL containing the word PASS, e.g. ..._FAIL_PASS (any FAIL-prefixed token makes the class FAIL)
a negated PASS, e.g. ..._NOT_PASS (negation tokens in the namespace)
any verdict with blocking_findings other than the integer 0, including a string '0' or an absent count
CERTIFICATION_PREDICATE.implementation: scripts/infra-read/certification.ts (assessCertificationEvent, terminalClassOf), called by protocol.ts measureDn0 for every configured event; run-governed-reads.ts dn0ConfigFor configures {path, packageId, certifiedCandidate} per event and NO verdict name.

RECERT_MATERIALIZATION_CONTRACT.CERTIFIED_CANDIDATE.candidate_head: The exact 40-hex HEAD the recertification reviewed. The execution protocol is invoked with the same SHA as --certified-candidate; any other value fails LIMB_1.
RECERT_MATERIALIZATION_CONTRACT.VERDICT: verdict = the certifier's own token, copied verbatim, whatever its namespace; blocking_findings = the integer count reported.
RECERT_MATERIALIZATION_CONTRACT.who_writes_it: The executing lane, from the certifier's output, before DN-0. measured: The IC measured that on Windows Gh_Token / Vercel_Token bypass a case-sensitive denylist and are seen by the child as GH_TOKEN / VERCEL_TOKEN (Windows environment names are case-insensitive).

This lane measured, by NAME only, that the caller environment of the executor host carries CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, which the v1.0.4 denylist model passed to both provider CLIs; it also carries NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA, GIT_EDITOR and VERCEL_PLUGIN_* variables. No proxy variable is set on the host. No value was read.

Under the constructed environment below, offline: gh config get git_protocol -h github.com resolves (exit 0) and vercel --version runs (exit 0, 54.14.2). Keyring and auth-file resolution depend only on the account-context variables that ARE carried.
ENVIRONMENT_MODEL.rule: NORMATIVE. gh and vercel receive a CONSTRUCTED environment, never the caller's environment minus a denylist. Names are compared in UPPER CASE everywhere. Two case variants of one allowed name with different values are refused (STOP_ENV_AMBIGUOUS). At invocation time, independently of the builder, every name is upper-cased and refused if credential-shaped (STOP_CREDENTIAL_OVERRIDE_IN_ENV) or outside the allowlist (STOP_ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED).

decided_not_carried.credential_names: any name whose upper-cased form contains TOKEN, SECRET, PASSW, API_KEY / APIKEY, PRIVATE_KEY, CREDENTIAL, COOKIE or AUTH. Refused at invocation even if a builder regression put one back.
decided_not_carried.NODE_OPTIONS: REFUSED. It can preload arbitrary code into the Vercel CLI process (--require / --import), which runs with the OWNER credential.
decided_not_carried.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS / NODE_TLS_REJECT_UN: REFUSED. They widen the TLS trust the credential is presented under. NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA is set on the host; dropping it narrows Node to its bundled public roots, which chain the public provider APIs. A TLS failure then signals interception instead of being accepted.
decided_not_carried.GH_CONFIG_DIR / GH_HOST / GH_REPO / VERC: REFUSED. They redirect which identity, host, project or configuration the CLI resolves. The measured identity (RC-9a) is the one resolved from the default account locations, and nothing else may be substituted for it.
decided_not_carried.HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY / N: REFUSED. None is set on the executor host. If the network ever requires one, the read fails visibly rather than routing a credential through caller-chosen infrastructure.
decided_not_carried.DEBUG / GH_DEBUG: REFUSED. Diagnostic modes print request detail.

ENVIRONMENT_MODEL.owner_decision_needed: NO. Both viable choices for proxies and extra CA material (carry or refuse) were evaluated; refusing has no trust cost and only an availability cost that fails visibly, so no two choices with materially different TRUST consequences remain.

ENTROPY_DISPOSITION.measured: Over the committed authority files of this PR the OPAQUE_HIGH_ENTROPY detector fires on separator-segmented identifiers such as a v1.0.0 key made of 'class_for_' followed by the six labels DN-7 .. DN-12 joined with underscores (quoted in pieces here because this file must itself scan CLEAN; the whole identifier is pinned in tests/infra-read/evidence-scan.test.ts) and two similar keys in the parent DAG amendment. No production or evidence file of this lane triggers it.
ENTROPY_DISPOSITION.why_not_refined: The only discriminator between those identifiers and a token is segment structure. Exempting strings with 3 or more separators would also exempt about 13% of uniformly random 40-character base64url tokens (P(X>=3) for X ~ Binomial(40, 2/64) is about 0.128). That is a material weakening, and security takes precedence over convenience.
ENTROPY_DISPOSITION.operational_consequence: An evidence record whose projection legitimately contains such an identifier would fail the post-projection scan and stop the phase. That fails closed, and the known false-positive shape is pinned by a test so it is visible rather than surprising.

DN0_FETCH_DISPOSITION.why_separate_from_X_R1: X-R1 is a governed READ of provider state: it runs in an EMPTY isolated directory with every configuration source removed, because its semantics are fully stated on its argv. The DN-0 fetch is a freshness refresh of the executing repository: its semantics (which remote, which refspecs, prune) come FROM repository configuration, and the host's system configuration sets the TLS backend (http.sslbackend, MEASURED). Applying XCC-1's system/global/repository isolation would change what the fetch does. XCC-1 is therefore not extended to it.
DN0_FETCH_DISPOSITION.what_is_applied: Everything that can be applied without changing semantics for a public repository: argv resets credential.helper, core.askPass and http.extraHeader to empty; environment GIT_ASKPASS and SSH_ASKPASS empty, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never. A public repository needs no credential, so these change nothing unless a credential would otherwise have been presented, in which case the fetch now FAILS instead.
residual_vectors_checked_before_the_fetc: URL rewrite and cookie file. The resets cannot neutralize url.*.insteadOf / pushInsteadOf (which can put userinfo into the fetched URL) or http.*.cookieFile. Their absence at every scope is required: git config --name-only --get-regexp for those keys must exit 1, else STOP_DN0_FETCH_CREDENTIAL_VECTOR and no fetch. MEASURED on the executor host at this lane: exit 1.

Remote shape. An ssh remote presents a key and a userinfo URL presents a token, neither of which the resets touch. remote.origin.url must match the value pattern https-without-userinfo: git config --name-only --get-regexp on that key with that value pattern must exit 0, else STOP_DN0_FETCH_CREDENTIAL_VECTOR and no fetch. MEASURED on the executor host at this lane: exit 0.
DN0_FETCH_DISPOSITION.values_never_observed: Both probes use --name-only and a value pattern, so git prints at most a key NAME. A credential-bearing configuration value is refused without ever entering the executor process (DF11: the credential MUST NEVER be observed).
DN0_FETCH_DISPOSITION.residual_not_eliminated: NONE identified for credential presentation by the fetch. The fetch still reads repository and system configuration by design; that is the documented semantic difference from X-R1, not a credential path.
DN0_FETCH_DISPOSITION.no_remote_mutation: The fetch only updates local remote-tracking refs.
